subject: Commit fulfillment tiers & sweep policy (Helix Payments)
messages:
From: Maria Gonzales <maria.gonzales@helixpay.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@helixpay.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial commit drawdown proposal + sweep policy question

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to share our draft of the committed spend structure so we can align on mechanics before legal starts redlines. We're targeting a 24-month engagement with an annual committed prepay that scales across two years. Key points from our side: 

- Commit: $1,500,000 per year (we're open to a multi-year blended discount).
- Expected consumption profile: 40% of Year 1 in months 1–6 (pilot + integration), 60% of Year 1 in months 7–12 (ramp), with Year 2 smoothing out to a steady monthly run rate.
- We prefer a monthly drawdown from the prepay wallet rather than quarterly debits.
- Sweep request: any unused monthly balance should carry forward, but procurement wants a formal "sweep" that will reclaim >60% unused funds after month 12 unless usage ramps.

Open questions for Redwood:
1) Can you support a tranche-release schedule so we only unlock more of the prepay wallet as usage milestones are met?
2) What holdback percentage do you typically use for multi-year commitments and how does that affect discounts?
3) If there is a true-up, do you invoice overage at list or at a negotiated overage rate?

I've attached our internal commit schedule for context (Helix_Commit_Schedule_v2.pdf). Legal will add the SOW and billing cadence once mechanics are agreed.

Appreciate a short call if helpful — Maria

Attachments: Helix_Commit_Schedule_v2.pdf (1 page, XLSX->PDF export)

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gonzales <maria.gonzales@helixpay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial commit drawdown proposal + sweep policy question

Hi Maria — thanks for the clear summary and the commitment schedule. Looping in Ben (sales lead) and Lauren (finance ops) so we can confirm finance and operational constraints. High level response below; I've also attached a short proposed mechanics doc to accelerate legal (redlined_SOW.docx).

Short answers to your questions: 
1) Tranche-release: Yes — we can do tranche-based releases tied to usage milestones. A common structure we use is a time-and-usage hybrid: an initial release equal to 35% of the annual wallet at contract start, then incremental releases at months 4, 8, and 12 contingent on hitting usage thresholds. If Helix expects a frontloaded pilot, we can front-load the initial tranche to 50% and compress later releases.

2) Holdback and discounts: For a two-year commitment we typically hold back 10–15% of the total prepay as a contractual reserve. Holdback size moves the pricing band — 10% holdback aligns with the mid-tier discount (approx 18–20% off list in Year 1), 15% holdback maps to deeper protection / a slightly higher blended list price. We can model a blended discount schedule: Year 1 = 20% off list, Year 2 = 12% off list with a guaranteed blended effective discount across the term.

3) True-up and overage: We invoice monthly against the wallet drawdown. Any usage beyond the wallet is billed monthly as an overage. For committed customers we typically offer an overage rate at 65–85% of list (depends on holdback/commit size). If you prefer a fixed overage cap for budgeting, we can include that as a term (for example, capped at 75% of list).

A few other operational notes: 
- Sweep mechanics: We recommend a 2-stage sweep rather than an immediate reclaim. After month 12 we move to an aggressive reclaim cadence for balances >60% unused (this protects capacity planning). Prior to month 12 we allow carry-forward.
- Early termination: Pro rata credit of unspent wallet less a 10% administrative retention is our standard; larger deals can negotiate a lower retention.
- Invoicing cadence: Redwood prefers monthly invoicing against the wallet for transparency; we can accommodate quarterly invoices if Helix requires it for AR processes.

Next steps: 
- If this high-level approach looks acceptable, Ben and I will prepare an illustrated tranche schedule and a single-page summary for your procurement/legal to sign off.
- Proposed call: Thu 12 Nov, 10am PT. Does that work for you?

Thanks,
Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: redlined_SOW.docx (term sheet + SOW, tracked changes)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 16:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial commit drawdown proposal + sweep policy question

Sofia / Lauren — quick internal note before the call with Helix: 

I agree with Sofia's monthly drawdown + tranche-release approach, but I want to propose one change to the tranche sizing to match typical ramp profiles we see in payments customers: a 30/50/20 release over the first 12 months (30% upfront, additional 50% by month 6 contingent on integration milestones, and final 20% at month 12 subject to a 60% usage trigger). That gives Helix runway for the pilot while protecting Redwood against heavy frontloaded consumption.

Couple of items for finance/legal to confirm: 
- Invoice cadence: finance would prefer monthly statements with a monthly ledger export. Lauren, can we confirm Redwood's ability to provide CSV ledger exports on a monthly basis to Helix?
- Accounting treatment of holdback: if we keep a 10% holdback as Sofia suggested, finance needs the contractual wording to specify that holdback is not recognized until 12 months unless released by usage milestones.
- Overage cap: recommend we offer a capped overage rate at 75% of list — simpler for procurement to budget and acceptable margin for us.

If everyone is aligned I'll push an updated one-pager and a single-term-sheet for signature. I also think we should include a short operational playbook (billing, support SLAs, contact roster) as an appendix to the SOW.

Ben Carter
Director, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0188
